newsitem.title: USA: GPU files pilot electricity program in N.J.
newsitem.headline: GPU files pilot electricity program in N.J.

text.p: GPU Energy said it filed a proposal Friday with the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (BPU) outlining a pilot program aimed at giving electricity customers a choice of power supplier.
The move comes amid New Jersey's efforts to deregulate its electricity industry, introducing open competition among utilities for customers.
New Jersey's Monroe Township, in Middlesex County, was named as the first participant in the program, the company said in a statement.

"The pilot filed today is an 'energy supply only' program, which is not contingent on the outcome of a particular restructuring with the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnection," GPU Energy said.

Members of the PJM power pool are currently debating how best to independently operate PJM to ensure reliable electricity supplies despite open competition among the companies generating and transmitting power over the system.
GPU Energy said it plans to help Monroe County officials seek and review proposals from other power suppliers wishing to join the open retail program.
It will also continue to provide the needed capacity and infrastructure to maintain system reliability, as well as meter reading and a unified billing service for the participating customers.

According to the proposal, the pilot program would last one year, at which time Monroe Township will review and possibly renew it. GPU said it expected the pilot to be launched some time in the second quarter of 1997.
"This...represents the first real test of electric retail competition in New Jersey, and will be a valuable learning experience for everyone," said GPU Energy vice president Glenn Steiger.
"By implementing this...as an energy-only program, many of the still to be resolved issues can be avoided."
Monroe officials, who have been working with GPU Energy on the plan since August, said they anticipated the program would trim electricity bills in the township by five to 10 percent.
GPU Energy, formerly Jersey Central Power & Light (JCP&L), is based in Morristown, N.J.
